aspect: Total collapse is a recurring event
description: Nigeria suffered a total blackout on 14 September 2023 when the national grid collapsed, with distribution companies citing system failure. The grid collapsed twelve times in the first half of 2024 alone, with further failures into 2026.
energy_note: The whole country's electricity, off, twelve times in six months.

aspect: The outage hours, against the regional average
description: Sub-Saharan outages averaged 56 hours per month in 2024; Nigeria's industrial clusters regularly exceed 200 hours.
energy_note: Two hundred hours a month without power, in the industrial areas.

aspect: So the generator is the actual grid
description: A dense ecosystem of distributors with nationwide financing, parts and maintenance networks sustains generator dependence. Every outage drives further generator investment, and fuel subsidies long made that artificially competitive.
money_note: Annual generator purchase, fuel and maintenance.
energy_note: A second, private, petrol-powered national grid.

aspect: EXAMPLE - fifty-seven thousand naira a week, for a barber
description: One Lagos barber described spending N57,000 on generator fuel in a single week while unable to raise haircut prices without losing customers - the squeeze in its simplest form.
energy_note: A week's fuel, and the same price per haircut.

aspect: Women's unpaid work absorbs the schedule
description: Cooking, laundry, water pumping, phone charging and children's homework are scheduled around whenever the power is on, including at night. The household manager does the absorbing.
time_note: Days per year of rescheduled domestic labour.
energy_note: Doing the washing at 2am because that is when it came on.

aspect: It sets a ceiling on which industries can exist
description: No cold chain, no reliable manufacturing, no data centre, no synchronous remote work at scale. The power schedule is an industrial policy nobody wrote.
energy_note: Whole sectors, ruled out by a generator.

description: She sells frozen fish. Six hours of grid power a day and a generator that costs NGN 9,000 a day to run against a margin that does not support it. In August she loses a full freezer and with it the working capital for the month.
energy_note: A business model destroyed by a power schedule.

aspect: A generation grows up scheduling around it
description: Children raised on the power schedule study when the light is on rather than when they are able to concentrate, charge everything the moment it returns, and carry the habit into countries where it is unnecessary. It reads there as anxiety.
energy_note: Charging everything at once, in a country where you needn't.
